# Diagnose usage

Anthropic's Claude Code team reviewed the session IDs people shared in late October 2026 and found no single root cause and no regression. Most fast drains traced to one or two heavy sessions, plus a few smaller token-burn issues Anthropic said it was rolling out fixes for. This skill follows that finding: locate the heavy session first, and treat a product bug as the last explanation, not the first.

## Ground rules

- **Find the session before the setting.** Fast drains usually come from one or two sessions. Changing global settings for all work fixes the wrong thing and makes everything else worse.
- **Never promise a bug or a fix.** Say "update Claude Code, then re-check `/usage`", not "this is a known bug". Anthropic did not find a single cause.
- **Don't run slash commands for the user.** `/usage`, `/effort` and `/feedback` are built-ins the user types. Ask for the pasted output; do not guess at numbers.
- **Check names before you say them.** Effort levels, flags and features in Claude Code change month to month. If a level, flag or command is not in the user's paste or the current docs, say you could not confirm it. The docs map is in the `product-self-knowledge` skill when it is installed.

## Workflow

1. Ask once, in one message: which session or day, when the drain started, and which of these they used: goal mode, workflows, agent teams, subagents, an SDK or headless job, a raised effort level. Skip anything they already said.
2. Ask the user to run `/usage` and paste the result. It shows where a session's tokens went; without it any ranking is a guess.
3. Open `references/burn-sources.md` and match the evidence in the paste to its suspects. Rank by tokens in the paste, not by the order in the file.
4. Report in the shape below.
5. If nothing in the paste explains the drain, or it still looks wrong after the change, tell the user to run `/feedback` from that session. Anthropic said it follows up directly with people who share a session ID.

`references/trigger-cases.md` holds the test cases. Open it only when tuning the description above.

## Report

Up to three culprits, ranked. Each one: what the paste shows, why that costs a lot, and one change. Then one next step. Mark which findings came from the user's paste and which are general causes you could not confirm from it.

## Hand off

- Setting an effort level or fan-out for the next heavy task goes to `choose-effort`, as does "how do I use less from now on" when there is no past session to look at.
- What a plan allows, what it costs, API billing go to `product-self-knowledge`.

# Burn sources

Open this at step 3 of the workflow, once you have the user's `/usage` paste.

**Provenance.** The first five suspects come from Boris Cherny's (Claude Code) X post of 29 Oct 2026 on usage draining faster than expected. The effort-setting mechanics under "How effort is set" come from third-party write-ups of the Claude Code docs, checked 29 Oct 2026. Both can be out of date: confirm against the user's `/effort` slider and the current docs before stating a level or flag as fact.

## Suspects

| Suspect | Why it is heavy | Evidence to look for in the paste | One change |
|---|---|---|---|
| High effort (xhigh, max) | Deeper reasoning per turn, more tokens per turn | One long session at a raised level | Lower the level for routine work; `/effort auto` returns to the model default |
| Subagents inheriting effort | Anthropic says subagents inherit the session's effort by default, so a raised level multiplies across every subagent | Many short agent runs under one session | Lower the session effort before fan-out. Whether a per-subagent effort setting is honoured has been reported both ways; test it, do not assume |
| Goal mode (`/goal`) | Keeps working until a condition is met, so one prompt can mean many turns | A single session far larger than the rest | Bound the goal, and check `/usage` partway |
| Workflows and Agent Teams | Fan out many agents at once | A burst of agent activity in one session | Use only when the work parallelises; check `/usage` after the first stage |
| Long SDK jobs | Headless loops run unattended and accumulate | A job session far above interactive ones | Set a turn or budget cap if the SDK version offers one; look up the option name in the docs, do not invent it |
| Environment override | A `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` variable is reported to override every other effort setting | User says they set a low level but usage did not change | Ask the user to check that variable in their shell and CI |
| Heavier model | Model and effort are set separately and cost combines both | `/model` shows a larger model than the work needs | Ask whether the task needs it; `/model` changes it |

## How effort is set

Per the third-party summaries, not verified against the live docs:

- `/effort` opens a slider; `/effort <level>` sets directly; `/effort auto` resets to the model default.
- `claude --effort <level>` sets it for one launched session.
- Levels run low, medium, high, xhigh, max, and a Claude Code setting called ultracode. Which levels exist depends on the model, and an unsupported level falls back to a lower one without telling you.
- Max applies to the current session only.

## Reading the paste

Pick the one or two sessions or categories holding the most tokens. If the top one is not a suspect above, say so and go to step 5 (`/feedback`) rather than forcing a match.

content.text:
The cause is one prompt: your 13:15 refactor request. Together, the subagents and the workflow took 74% of the window. The main conversation took only 21%. This ranking comes straight from your paste. The mechanisms are general causes. I couldn't confirm them from the paste.

**1. Subagents inheriting xhigh and Opus (61%)**
- The paste shows 14 subagents, one per file. Your settings are effort `xhigh` and model `opus`, with subagent model `inherit`. Opus accounts for 88% of the session.
- Anthropic says subagents inherit the session's effort by default. If that holds here, each of the 14 ran deep reasoning on your most expensive model, 14 times over.
- **Change:** before a fan-out like this, lower the effort with `/effort` (or `/effort auto` to return to the model default). Set the subagent model to Sonnet instead of `inherit`. Per-file refactors rarely need Opus. I couldn't confirm the exact setting name from your paste, so check the docs for it.

**2. The refactor-sweep workflow (13%)**
- It fanned out across 14 files from a single prompt, and you were away at lunch. Nothing stopped it or let you check the cost partway.
- The paste doesn't show whether the 13% includes the workflow's own agents or only its coordination. Some of it may overlap with the subagent figure.
- **Change:** run it on one or two files first. Check `/usage`, then expand. Only fan out when the files really are independent.

**3. A global xhigh default since 3 Nov (a likely contributor)**
- xhigh was set globally in `~/.claude/settings.json`. It raises the cost of every turn, including the 21% in your main conversation, and it multiplies everything above.
- I can't tell from the paste what it cost over the past ten days. Your normal day uses about 30% of a window, so it's probably fine for ordinary work.
- **Change:** keep your default at a lower level. Raise it per task for hard problems. Also check that `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` isn't set in your shell. It's reported to override other effort settings.

**Next step:** you're at 96% and the window resets at 17:10. Either wait, or switch to Sonnet at a lower effort for small tasks. Also check that the workflow isn't still running. After the reset, rerun the refactor in stages as described above. If the next heavy session still burns far more than this breakdown explains, run `/feedback` from it. Anthropic said it follows up with people who share a session ID.
